until the cloud (BatonDeck, a private repository) removed it on 2026-09-29 and decided through this
library (batondeck ba68f9c, a hash of its history before the rewrite of 2026-10-01); `js/cases/limits-vectors.json`, a fixed record made on 2026-09-28 by
running that TypeScript over SQLite, holds every port to its decisions and to the bits of every row
it wrote.
Two rules have no TypeScript to be held to: the guest total, charged before the open, and the cap on
waiting requests.

| Function | Input | Output | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `limits_rules_check` | `rules` | `ok`: true<br>or `ok`: false, `why`: string<br>*fails:* `bad_request` | Whether a rules document can be enforced as written, and the first reason it cannot, in this order: not an object (`the limits rules are an object`); a member it does not hold, the first in sorted order (`the limits rules hold <members>, and nothing else: <member>`); each member in the order of `LimitsRules`, absent or not a number (`<member> is a number`); then every number finite, `contact_calls_per_second` above 0 (`… is above 0`) and every other at least 1 (`… is at least 1`); `pending_in_cap` whole (`pending_in_cap is a whole number`); and a contact's bucket refilling from empty within the hour (`contact_burst / contact_calls_per_second is at most 3600: …`). `rules` absent or null is `bad_request`, `rules is required`. A host publishes no document this refuses. |
| `limits_decide` | `rules`: LimitsRules, `charge`: LimitsCharge, `now`: integer, `state`?: object\|null | `allowed`: boolean, `retry_after`: integer\|null, `refused_by`: string\|null, `writes`: [`bucket`: string, `tokens`: number, `updated_at`: integer]<br>*fails:* `bad_request` | SPEC §12's call budgets as one decision (crates/hdtp-limits; go/limits.go). A call is charged one token in EVERY bucket of its charge, or in none: a refusal spends nothing. A bucket's level is `min(burst, tokens + elapsed × rate)`, `elapsed` the seconds since `updated_at` and never negative (a clock that went back refills nothing, and the row is written with the earlier time); a level under 1 refuses, with `retry_after = max(1, ceil((1 − level) / rate))`. The arithmetic is what the cloud's `RateLimiter.take` was, operation for operation in IEEE double precision, until the cloud removed it and decided through this function (batondeck ba68f9c); `js/cases/limits-vectors.json`, a fixed record of that TypeScript's decisions, holds every port to the same decisions and the same bits. A host may delete a row idle for over an hour: under rules `limits_rules_check` passes it is full, and no decision changes. In order: `rules` (absent: `rules is required`; not enforceable: `the limits rules cannot be enforced: <limits_rules_check's why>`), `charge` (not an object: `charge is required`; `charge.kind is required`; `charge.kind is one of …`; a member its kind does not hold, the first in sorted order: `a <kind> charge holds <members>, and nothing else: <member>`; `charge.<member> is required` for a string that is absent or empty, `charge.<member> is a whole number` for a count, `charge.root is a string or null`, `charge.source is required`, `charge.addressed is required`), `now` (absent or null: `now is required`; otherwise `now is a time in milliseconds`: a whole number from 0 to 2^53 − 1, written without a fraction or an exponent), `state` (not an object: `state is an object of rows by bucket`; a row, in sorted order of key, that does not read: `the state's row <key> does not read: <member>`). |
| `limits_buckets` | `rules`: LimitsRules, `charge`: LimitsCharge | `buckets`: [`key`: string, `per_second`: number, `burst`: number]<br>*fails:* `bad_request` | The rows `limits_decide` reads for a charge, so a host can fetch them before it asks: the key scheme `LimitsCharge` describes, from the one place it is written (crates/hdtp-limits `Charge::buckets`; go/limits.go `Buckets`), where a host on the Wasm had to derive it a second time. Reads `rules` and then `charge` exactly as `limits_decide` does, in its words (`rules is required`; `the limits rules cannot be enforced: <why>`; the charge's own refusals). |

## 7. Gates

1. `cargo test` and `go test ./...` each: rebuild the seven vector certificates byte for byte from
   `leaf_keys_pkcs8_hex` and the labelled seeds (root keys are derived from `seed("root/alina")` etc.,
   exactly as `gen.mjs`), prove every chain case, newest-leaf case, `certificate_renewed` case and
   `v: 1` envelope, and reproduce the three envelopes' `enc`/`ct` from their ephemeral seeds.
2. `js/check.mjs` runs the same proof through a port in Node, reading vectors from the specification as the
   seed's `check.mjs` does: `--port wasm` (default) or `--port go`. **Both**, because for a long time
   only the first was run and the second was failing three assertions unseen — the three that re-seal
   a vector from its ephemeral seed and compare the bytes, which is the only check proving a port's
   envelopes are the vectors' envelopes.
3. `js/intrude.mjs` replays every scenario of `hdtp-spec/vectors/intrude.mjs` with Mallory built
   on the seed library and the defender on a port: `--port wasm` (default) or `--port go`. Every
   scenario's verdict must match the seed's: blocked, residual, never REPRODUCES — and the run fails
   if the two suites do not hold the same scenarios, so neither side's count is written down here.
4. `node --test contract/schema.test.mjs` holds the contract's own validator to a value per keyword
   that must fail it, and asserts it REFUSES a keyword it does not implement — a validator that
   ignored one would let `contract.json` state a constraint nothing holds, which is worse than
   stating nothing.
5. `js/parity.mjs` is a **gate**, not a courtesy. It feeds both ports the same arguments — a missing
   member, a member that is `null`, bytes that will not decode, an explicit `valid_days: 0`, a
   mismatched `sig_alg`, a name that straddles the vCard fold, every private and loopback spelling of
   an address, a root offered as a key id — and compares the whole answer, `why` strings included.
   The vectors prove the bytes a peer sees; this proves the codes, the words and the shapes a
   *caller* sees, which no vector carries. Besides the cases written by hand, `js/cases/generated.mjs`
   makes, for every function this file declares, the shapes of a caller's mistake from the function's
   own `params`: `{}`; the hostile object `js/cases/hostile.json` (which the Go port's
   `TestCallNeverPanics` sweeps with too); each required member absent and `null`, held to §0's
   `<name> is required`; each optional string `""`; each optional member of the wrong type; a member
   the contract does not declare; and, for read order, each required member absent beside each other
   member of the wrong type. Each is varied from a call that succeeds on both ports, named per
   function. Every case must pass: nothing is excused. It also fails when:
   - the two dispatchers and `contract/contract.json` stop naming the same set of functions
     (`version` lived in one dispatcher and not the other until this check existed; a function
     described in the contract and dispatched by neither port would be prose nothing runs);
   - an answer does not hold to the shape the contract declares for it, from EITHER port — the one
     check here that two agreeing ports cannot pass by agreeing, since a member both grew, or both
     dropped, is invisible to a comparison;
   - a function on either dispatcher has no case here, so the contract cannot grow past its guard;
   - an error code a function declares is never produced by both ports in one case they answered
     alike — a refusal nobody compared, or a code nothing can reach, which is a claim to take out of
     this file;
   - a function is only ever compared through a list of named keys rather than whole. That last one
     is the point: `card_decode` dropped its entire `leaf` member in one port, and a key list would
     never have noticed, because a key list only looks at the keys someone thought to name. Where an
     answer carries something genuinely per-run — a random serial, a fresh ephemeral — the case
     passes a function that replaces that one value with a description of it, and everything else is
     still compared. Narrowing a case to `['error']` to make a disagreement go away is not a fix: a
     differing `why` *is* the finding.
6. `wasm-bindgen-test` in headless Chrome for the browser build. A host that runs `pkg-web` in a
   Worker or a page tests it there, in its own repository, against the bytes it vendored.

---

## Appendix: the domain types

Generated from `contract/contract.json`'s `$defs`, which is where the tables above get their words.
A type used in an argument and in an answer is one definition, which is the point of having the
file: `Fingerprint` cannot mean `sha256:…` in one function's row and something else in another's.

| Type | Shape | |
|---|---|---|
| `ErrorCode` | bad_request\|parse\|unsupported\|envelope_invalid\|vault\|root_expired\|key\|internal | Why a call failed. `bad_request`: an argument is missing or unusable as asked. `parse`: bytes that are there and will not read. `unsupported`: an algorithm or a function this library does not have. `envelope_invalid`: SPEC §12's code, for an envelope that does not open or prove itself. `vault`: the vault refused. `root_expired`: a wallet asked to sign under a root past its `notAfter` (SPEC §2.2) — the library's refusal, never a code on the wire; a verifier meeting such a root in a chain refuses it by rule 4 of `validate_chain`. `key` and `internal` are declared so a caller's switch has a name for them; no input known reaches either. |
| `B64url` | string | Bytes, as base64url without padding, in exactly this alphabet. Every answer spells them this way, and every wire object of the specification is read this strictly: an envelope's members, an export's certificates, a signing request. A library argument outside those objects is also read with padding or the standard alphabet, and never with whitespace (CONTRACT §0); a card's certificate loses its spaces, tabs, CRs and LFs before it is read (`card_decode`). |
| `Alg` | ed25519\|p256 | A key algorithm. A key of any other is refused where it is read (CONTRACT §0). |
| `Fingerprint` | string | `"sha256:" + b64url(SHA-256(SPKI))`, in its one spelling: the last character's two spare bits are zero (RFC 4648 §3.5). |
| `Instant` | string | An RFC 3339 UTC instant with second precision, as every answer writes one. |
| `InstantIn` | string | An RFC 3339 UTC instant as an argument, in the one grammar every port reads: upper-case T and Z, no offset, `.` alone before a fraction of a second, which is allowed and DROPPED, because the boundary is whole seconds. |
| `Pkcs8` | B64url | A private key: PKCS #8 DER. |
| `Spki` | B64url | A public key: SubjectPublicKeyInfo DER. |
| `CertDer` | B64url | One X.509 certificate, DER. |
| `Chain` | [CertDer] | `[leaf, root]`. |
| `Tbs` | B64url | A TBSCertificate, DER: the bytes an external signer signs. |
| `SigAlg` | B64url | An AlgorithmIdentifier, DER — the TBS's own third field. |
| `Csr` | B64url | A PKCS #10 CertificationRequest, DER. |
| `Serial` | B64url | A certificate serial number, 8 to 20 bytes. Absent, the core draws 8 random bytes. |
| `Seed32` | B64url | Exactly 32 bytes. |
| `Suite` | HDTP-SEAL-P256\|HDTP-SEAL-X25519 | An HPKE suite (§5). |
| `Form` | chain\|leaf | How the sender proves itself inside the plaintext: its whole chain, or the fingerprint of a leaf the recipient already holds. |
| `Key` | `alg`: Alg, `pkcs8`: Pkcs8, `spki`: Spki, `fingerprint`: Fingerprint |  |
| `Envelope` | `protected`: B64url, `enc`: B64url, `ct`: B64url, `sig`: B64url | A sealed envelope: its four members (SPEC §13.1). |
| `ArrivedEnvelope` | `protected`: string, `enc`: string, `ct`: string, `sig`: string | An envelope as it ARRIVED: four strings, which may be anything. Judging their spelling is the function's work, not the caller's. |
| `Certificate` | `kind`: root\|leaf\|other, `subject`: string, `issuer`: string, `serial`: B64url, `not_before`: Instant, `not_after`: Instant, `alg`: Alg, `spki`: Spki, `fingerprint`: Fingerprint, `key_id`: B64url, `ski`: B64url \| null, `aki`: B64url \| null, `ca`: boolean, `path_len`: integer\|null, `key_usage`: [integer], `eku`: [string], `uris`: [string], `dns`: [string], `sig_alg`: string, `extensions`: [`id`: string, `critical`: boolean], `profile_error`: string\|null, `bytes`: integer | A certificate read back. `profile_error` judges it as a root when it is self-issued and a CA, otherwise as a leaf. |
| `ChainAccepted` | `ok`: true, `leaf_spki`: Spki, `leaf_fingerprint`: Fingerprint, `root_fingerprint`: Fingerprint, `endpoint`: string, `not_before`: Instant, `not_after`: Instant, `alg`: Alg |  |
| `ChainRefused` | `ok`: false, `rule`: integer, `reason`: string |  |
| `Pin` | `root`: Fingerprint, `endpoint`: string, `leaf`: string, `state`?: active\|pending_out\|blocked, `leaf_fingerprint`?: string | A contact as the host holds it. `state` absent is `active`; any other value but the three is refused, as is a `leaf_fingerprint` that is not a fingerprint (NodeState). |
| `HeldKey` | `kid`: Fingerprint, `leaf`: CertDer, `pkcs8`: Pkcs8, `current`?: boolean |  |
| `Tombstone` | `root`: Fingerprint, `leaf`: string, `at`: string |  |
| `FormerEndpoint` | `root`: Fingerprint, `endpoint`: string, `at`: string |  |
| `Windows` | {"skew_s":300,"max_lifetime_s":2592000,"tombstone_s":2592000,"claim_window_s":2592000,"max_leaf_days":398,"signing_max_ahead_s":600} | The protocol's windows, in seconds unless named otherwise, as both ports hold them (a test in each holds its constants to these, and a host that needs one reads it here): `skew_s`, how far a received envelope's `ts` may be from now, and `max_lifetime_s`, the most `exp − ts` may be (SPEC §13.3); `tombstone_s`, how long a removal tombstone holds a returning root at `ask` (§5.3), and `claim_window_s`, how long an endpoint stays claimed by the root that was pinned at it (§5.2) — each an age strictly under the window; `max_leaf_days`, the longest leaf a verifier accepts (§14.2); `signing_max_ahead_s`, the furthest ahead a signing request may expire (§9.1). |
| `CanonicalNumbers` | [["1e21","1e+21"],["1.5e300","1.5e+300"],["1e-7","1e-7"],["0.000001","0.000001"],["100.0","100"],["9223372036854775808.0","9223372036854776000"],["1e20","100000000000000000000"],["0.1","0.1"],["-0.0","0"],["42","42"],["1e-5","0.00001"],["0.0000001","1e-7"],["1.25e-9","1.25e-9"],["-1e-7","-1e-7"],["1e100","1e+100"],["9007199254740992","9007199254740992"],["9007199254740993","9007199254740992"],["-9007199254740993","-9007199254740992"],["12345678901234567890","12345678901234567000"]] | How the canonical JSON of an envelope header and a vault's authenticated data writes a number (RFC 8785 §3.2.2.3: as ECMAScript's Number prints it). Each row is a JSON number as a caller may write it and the text both ports canonicalise it to; a test in each port runs every row. |
| `NodeState` | `endpoint`: string, `accept_new_hosts`?: auto\|ask, `chain`?: Chain, `keys`?: [HeldKey], `former`?: [string], `sibling_kids`?: [string], `pins`?: [Pin], `tombstones`?: [Tombstone], `former_endpoints`?: [FormerEndpoint], `seen`?: [string] | What the host knows, handed to `decide` whole. Every list absent is empty; `accept_new_hosts` absent is `auto`, and anything but `auto` or `ask` is refused (`node.accept_new_hosts is auto or ask`). Read member by member in this order, a held key as `kid`, `leaf`, `pkcs8`, `current`, a pin as `root`, `endpoint`, `leaf`, `state`, `leaf_fingerprint`, a tombstone as `root`, `leaf`, `at`, a former endpoint as `root`, `endpoint`, `at`: a member absent, null or of the wrong type where one is required is `bad_request` naming it by its path (`node.endpoint is required`, `node.keys[0].kid is required`, `node.seen[1] is required`), and a pin's, a tombstone's or a former endpoint's `root` that is not a fingerprint is `bad_request` `<path>.root is not a fingerprint` (`node.pins[0].root is not a fingerprint`), read where the root is: the host's damaged state, which read as a root nothing matched came back as an `address_claim` that was not a fingerprint. So, each where it is read, is a held key's `kid` that is not a fingerprint (`<path>.kid is not a fingerprint`), a pin's `state` other than `active`, `pending_out` or `blocked` (`<path>.state is active, pending_out or blocked`; one was read as `active`, so a blocked contact whose host wrote `Blocked` was a full contact), and a pin's `leaf_fingerprint` that is not a fingerprint (`<path>.leaf_fingerprint is not a fingerprint`; `""` was a claim matching no leaf in one port and no claim in the other). The typed `decide` and `decide_chain` ask the same of a typed caller's state first, in the reader's order, where a Go caller's zero values, a `state` or a `leaf_fingerprint` of `""`, are `active` and none. |
| `GuestWhy` | unknown root\|blocked\|superseded leaf | Why a caller proven by a chain is a guest: its root is not pinned (`unknown root`), its pin is blocked (`blocked`), or the leaf it signed with is older than the pinned one (`superseded leaf`, §14.3). The words are the seed's `receive()`'s. |

A guest carries its reason, `demote` and the address claim; a chain that fails a rule, or a leaf of the pinned one's notBefore that is not it, is `envelope_invalid` in `decide`'s words. |

| `ExportManifest` | `hdtp_export`: 1, `owner`: Fingerprint, `owner_name`: string, `exported_at`: InstantIn, `tool`: string, `counts`: `contacts`: integer, `threads`: integer, `messages`: integer, `media`: integer, `files`: `contacts.csv`?: Sha256Hex, `threads.csv`?: Sha256Hex, `messages.jsonl`?: Sha256Hex | manifest.json (SPEC §9.2), exactly these members. |
| `ContactRow` | `root`: Fingerprint, `endpoint`: string, `name`: string, `display_name`: string, `status`: active\|blocked\|pending_out, `was_active`: boolean, `permissions`: [string], `their_permissions`: [string], `leaf`?: CertDer \| null, `root_cert`?: CertDer \| null, `added`: InstantIn | One row of contacts.csv (SPEC §9.2), as JSON: the permissions as lists, was_active a boolean, an empty leaf or root_cert null. |
| `ThreadRow` | `id`: string, `contact`: Fingerprint, `topic`: string, `created_at`: InstantIn, `last_at`: InstantIn, `contact_name`?: string, `contact_display_name`?: string | One row of threads.csv (SPEC §9.2). A removed thread is one whose contact is no root of contacts.csv: a former contact's conversation, which carries the names the contact is known by; on any other thread the two names are empty, and export_read does not answer them. |
| `Attachment` | `file`: Sha256Hex, `filename`: string, `mime`: string, `size`: integer |  |
| `MessageRow` | `id`: string, `thread`: string, `contact`: string, `msg_id`: string, `direction`: in\|out, `sender`: agent\|human, `time`: InstantIn, `body`: string, `reply_to`?: string\|null, `status`: delivered\|queued\|failed\|read, `attachments`: [Attachment] | One line of messages.jsonl (SPEC §9.2): at most one attachment, and a message with one has an empty body. |
| `DirectoryEntry` | `name`: string, `size`: integer, `encrypted`: boolean, `mode`: integer | One entry of the zip's central directory, as the host read it: the name as stored, the uncompressed size the header states, whether the entry is encrypted (general-purpose flag bit 0), and its Unix mode (the external attributes' high 16 bits; 0 when there is none). |
| `LedgerEntry` | `root`: Fingerprint, `endpoint`: string, `not_before`: Instant, `not_after`: Instant, `issued_at`: Instant, `origin`?: string | One leaf the wallet issued: the endpoint and the dates, which is what every rule reads. Never the leaf itself, which is the host's to serve and grants nothing (SPEC §9). |
| `VaultRoot` | `fingerprint`: Fingerprint, `cn`: string, `alg`?: Alg, `cert`: CertDer, `created`: Instant, `pkcs8`?: Pkcs8, `holder`?: `{…}`, `rebound_at`?: integer | One identity the wallet holds. In the file it carries the root's key (`pkcs8`) or names the card that does (`holder`); in the record it carries neither, until the root is re-bound (SPEC §9): then `rebound_at` (ms) marks the entry and `pkcs8` stays with it. |
| `VaultPasskey` | `credential_id`: string | The credential a derived root belongs to (SPEC §2.1); not secret. |
| `VaultContact` | `root`: Fingerprint, `endpoint`: string, `name`?: string, `leaf`?: CertDer, `root_cert`?: CertDer, `added`?: Instant | The wallet's own copy of one contact (SPEC §9): pinned by root, at an endpoint, under the person's name; a leaf and the root certificate when the wallet has seen them. |
| `VaultPlaintext` | `v`: 1, `roots`: [VaultRoot], `prf`?: Seed32, `passkey`?: VaultPasskey | What the FILE seals: the root and nothing else (SPEC §9). `prf` is the §2.1 secret a derived root's record is opened with, for the wallet that has lost its credential. A `v` that is not 1 is refused at both ends and nothing converts. |
| `RecordPlaintext` | `v`: 1, `roots`?: [VaultRoot], `ledger`?: [LedgerEntry], `contacts`?: [VaultContact], `passkey`?: VaultPasskey, `backup_verified_at`?: integer | What the RECORD seals (SPEC §9): the ledger and the contact book, the roots without their keys — or with one, once a root has been re-bound — and what the wallet page keeps beside them. Under the store key of §2.1 for a wallet with a credential; beside the file, under the recovery key, for one without. |
| `LimitsRules` | `contact_calls_per_second`: number, `contact_burst`: number, `identity_capacity_per_second`: number, `guest_calls_per_hour`: number, `guest_source_calls_per_hour`: number, `stranger_calls_out_per_hour`: number, `integration_calls_per_hour`: number, `guest_total_calls_per_hour`: number, `pending_in_cap`: integer | The numbers of SPEC §12's call budgets, as a host keeps them in its configuration. Every member is required; the library holds no default. |
| `LimitsCharge` | `kind`: "contact_in", `root`: string, `contact_cap`: integer<br>or `kind`: "guest_in", `root`?: string\|null, `source`: string, `addressed`: boolean<br>or `kind`: "guest_total"<br>or `kind`: "contact_out", `root`: string, `contact_cap`: integer<br>or `kind`: "stranger_out"<br>or `kind`: "integration", `integration`: string, `contact`: string<br>or `kind`: "pending_in", `held`: integer | What one call is charged to. The bucket keys are the cloud's `rate_buckets` keys. |
| `LimitsRow` | `tokens`: number, `updated_at`: integer | A bucket's row: the tokens left when it was last charged, and when, in milliseconds. |
| `LimitsIdle` | 3600000 | How long, in milliseconds, a bucket's row may sit untouched before it is full whatever it budgets: a host may delete a row older than this, and `limits_rules_check` refuses rules whose contact bucket takes longer to refill from empty (crates/hdtp-limits `IDLE_MS`, go/limits.go `LimitsIdleMS`; a test in each holds it to this). |
